text:
Arjun: Heads up - after the CUDA driver bump on canary H100s we're seeing a solid p99 spike (20-35%) but only for seq_len ~4k-8k on model `x-lr` :eyes:
Maya: Confirmed on my side, canary pool same story. Other seq lens <2k and >12k look fine.
Gabi: Quick profiler snapshot shows a different kernel being selected for the attention forward path around those seq lengths (autotuner chose `attention_fwd_fast_v2` instead of `attention_fwd_v1`). KV cache hits are slightly slower too.
Arjun: Micro numbers i grabbed:
```
# chosen kernel: attention_fwd_fast_v2
seq_len: 4096
latency p50/p99: 62ms / 320ms
SM utilization: 62%
Warp efficiency: 72%
DRAM BW: 210 GB/s
```
Arjun: And older kernel profile from last week:
```
# kernel: attention_fwd_v1
seq_len: 4096
latency p50/p99: 58ms / 240ms
SM utilization: 78%
Warp efficiency: 88%
DRAM BW: 180 GB/s
```
Maya: So autotuner/kernel-ranking changed post-driver and it's picking a kernel with worse warp efficiency for this phys/seq combo. Probably a driver-alignment change exposed different heuristics. :thinking_face: 
Gabi: Short-term mitigation options: disable autotuner, pin kernel override for the model, or route affected traffic to a fallback model variant that uses old kernel path. Rolling driver rollback is last resort IMO.
Henry: Quick commands we can run to reproduce at scale:
```
perf_runner --model x-lr --seqlen 4096 --batch 1 --repeat 200 --nvprof --collect=sm_efficiency,dram_bw,warp
```
Maya: I prototyped a kernel override config we could push as a hotfix:
```
{
  "autotuner": {
    "enabled": true,
    "kernel_overrides": {
      "x-lr/attention": "attention_fwd_v1"
    }
  }
}
```
Maya: Or flip the flag entirely: `REDWOOD_AUTOTUNE=0` in the canary config to force deterministic kernels until we sort it.
Gabi: Rollback plan draft: 1) apply kernel override + set AUTOTUNE=0 in canary, 2) run perf_runner to validate p99 back to baseline, 3) roll to remaining canaries, 4) optional driver rollback if autotuner still misbehaves everywhere.
Eva: I'll open an NVIDIA ticket with driver + kernel lists and perf dumps. Also scheduling a rollback window at 02:00 UTC tonight if we need to revert drivers. Tagging infra oncall.
perf-bot: ALERT: route /generate (us-east-1) p99 increased 24% vs baseline over the last 10m :warning:
Arjun: For longer-term: we should add architecture-aware kernel scoring tweaks in the autotuner (score function that includes warp efficiency and mem-bound penalty for H100), and add a seq-length -> kernel whitelist for critical models.
Henry: Agreed. I'll add a test to the CI perf suite that exercises seq ranges 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192 on H100 images after driver upgrades. Failing tests should block driver rollout.
Gabi: I'll prepare the canary patch (kernel override + autotune=0) and a short runbook for oncall to execute if p99 stays up.
Maya: Thanks — I'll validate the patch in my local canary cluster and post numbers here.
Arjun: Awesome. Assigning follow-ups: @Eva -> NVIDIA ticket + rollback ops; @Gabi -> canary hotfix PR; @Henry -> perf CI test; @Maya -> validation numbers. :thumbsup: 
Eva: ack, starting ticket and ops checklist now.
Maya: Quick note: when you run nvprof/nsight please capture L2 hit rate and global load efficiency; those helped me pinpoint kernel mismatch last time.
Arjun: leaving logs and profiler traces in /shared/perf/1749654321/ for anyone who wants to dig in.
Gabi: ok pushing PR to staging, will update thread with results in ~15m. :rocket:
